stated: Repair the UK’s broken relationship with Europe by taking unilateral steps, seeking partnerships with EU agencies, negotiating comprehensive veterinary and plant health agreements, mutual recognition agreements, and ultimately aiming to join the Single Market, giving Britain’s farmers the ability to trade with European neighbours with minimal need for checks.

source.quote: Unlock British businesses’ global potential by bringing down trade barriers and building stronger future relationships with our closest trading partners, including by fixing our broken relationship with Europe as set out in chapter 22.

consolidated_from: Negotiate Veterinary and Plant Health Agreements with Europe

bearing_set.reason: Reducing UK-EU trade friction — particularly via veterinary/SPS agreements and ultimately Single Market membership — would lower import costs on food and consumer goods, directly affecting household food bills and the inflation basket.

The policy explicitly targets farmers' market access and viability; broader Single Market membership also carries material implications for labour mobility, wage dynamics, and employment conditions across export-facing sectors.

Rejoining the Single Market would reverse a material share of the post-Brexit productivity and trade drag (OBR/NIESR have modelled Brexit reducing long-run GDP by ~4%), directly moving the real living-standards and business-investment indicators.

Single Market membership requires substantial EU budget contributions (historically ~£10–15bn/year), a concrete fiscal cost; set against improved tax revenues from economic recovery — both mechanisms move the debt-path sustainability indicator in opposite directions, making the net effect material and contested.

membership_note: The policy's core mechanisms are trade-friction reduction (O2), aggregate market-access/productivity gains (O13), labour-market effects of free movement (O4), and the budget-contribution vs. revenue tradeoff of Single Market membership (O12). Effects on inequality (O14) and cohesion (O15) are too indirect and confounded to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
